sections.title: Asset Quality & Funding
sections.subtitle: Standalone basis, as disclosed in quarterly results

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For ICICI Bank Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For ICICI Bank Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

npaRatio.title: Gross and net NPA ratio
npaRatio.content:
Gross NPA ratio is non-performing advances as a percentage of gross advances; net NPA ratio deducts provisions already held against those bad loans, so it is the unprovided exposure still at risk.

For ICICI Bank Limited: this is the single most-watched asset-quality metric for an Indian bank -- both ratios have fallen steadily from the FY2018-2019 peak as the post-2015 corporate NPA cycle was worked through, with Gross NPA down to ~1.4% and Net NPA to ~0.33% by FY2026.

What to watch:

  • Gross NPA ticking up quarter-on-quarter (fresh slippages outpacing recoveries/write-offs)
  • The gap between gross and net widening or narrowing (a shrinking gap with a flat gross ratio means provisioning is not keeping pace)

casaCoverage.title: CASA ratio and provision coverage ratio
casaCoverage.content:
CASA ratio (average) is current and savings account deposits as a share of total deposits -- the bank's lowest-cost, stickiest funding. Provision coverage ratio is total provisions held as a percentage of gross NPAs -- how much of the recognised bad-loan pool is already reserved for.

For ICICI Bank Limited: a high CASA mix (low-to-mid 40s historically) is a direct funding-cost advantage that supports NIM, and provision coverage has stayed in the mid-70s to high-70s through FY2025-2026, well above regulatory minimums, leaving limited room for a coverage-driven profit boost but also limited balance-sheet risk.

What to watch:

  • CASA ratio drifting down (depositors shifting to higher-yielding term deposits, raising funding cost)
  • Provision coverage ratio falling at the same time as gross NPA rises (double deterioration)

nim.title: Net interest margin
nim.content:
NIM is net interest income as a percentage of interest-earning assets.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the core profitability metric of a lender; a few basis points move earnings materially.

What to watch:

  • NIM trend with the rate cycle
  • Funding cost versus lending yield

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For ICICI Bank Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue

totalIncome.title: Total income
totalIncome.content:
Net interest income plus fees and other operating income.

For ICICI Bank Limited: the top line for a financial; revenue in the ordinary sense does not apply.

What to watch:

  • Income growth versus cost growth
